steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social class and achievement: working-class students consistently achieve less well than middle-class students. External factors: material deprivation (poorer housing, less study space, no internet), cultural deprivation (Bernstein: restricted code vs elaborated code), cultural capital (Bourdieu: middle-class knowledge, tastes and values give advantage in school). Internal factors: streaming and labelling (Becker: teachers have an 'ideal pupil' image that is middle-class).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Gender and achievement: girls now outperform boys at every level (61% of girls vs 50% of boys achieve 5+ GCSEs A*-C). Reasons for girls' improvement: feminism (changed aspirations), changing family patterns (more women-headed households), employment opportunities (more jobs for women), GCSE coursework favoured girls. Reasons for boys' underachievement: laddish subcultures (Epstein: working-class boys see academic work as 'unmasculine'), male role model deficit (few male primary teachers).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethnicity and achievement: Chinese and Indian students achieve above the national average; Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Black Caribbean students achieve below. External factors: language barriers (English as additional language), material deprivation (higher poverty rates among some ethnic groups), family structure (more lone-parent families among Black Caribbean). Internal factors: teacher labelling (Gillborn and Youdell: teachers have lower expectations of Black students), institutional racism (policies that inadvertently disadvantage ethnic minorities), ethnocentric curriculum.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Labelling and self-fulfilling prophecy: Rosenthal and Jacobson's Pygmalion study showed that teacher expectations influenced student performance. Students labelled as 'bright' improved; those labelled as 'slow' declined. Becker: teachers judge students against the 'ideal pupil' (middle-class, compliant, motivated).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how social class affects educational achievement, using external and internal factors. | Evaluate why girls now outperform boys in education. | Assess the relative importance of external and internal factors in creating ethnic differences in educational achievement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Class: external (material + cultural deprivation) + internal (labelling, streaming). Both matter. Gender: girls NOW outperform boys. Causes: feminism, coursework, aspirations. Boys: laddish culture, role model deficit. Ethnicity: external (poverty, language) + internal (labelling, institutional racism, ethnocentric curriculum). Both interact.
